description: Low spreading native verbena with flat heads of intense scarlet flowers held just above the ground. The strongest red in the native palette.
nativeRange: Argentina, Uruguay, southern Brazil and neighbouring regions
ecology: A grassland groundcover of open, well-drained ground. Runs along the surface and roots as it goes, so it knits together the front of a planting.
wildlifeNotes: The scarlet flowers pull in butterflies and hummingbirds, and being low it covers the ground layer that taller nectar plants leave empty.
soil: Well-drained and lean; dislikes sitting wet
propagation: Spreads by rooting stems, and easy from cuttings.
